# Tártaros walks into a gaming, fantasy & entertainment ip firm

The gaming, fantasy & entertainment ip world does not cite Tártaros in its documentation. It does not need to — it performs the archetype daily, unbilled.

## Before the Office, the Story

**The Third Primordial.** When the world began, Hesiod names three things that came to be of themselves: Cháos, the yawning gap; Gaia, the broad-breasted earth; and 'dim Tártaros, in the depths of the broad-pathed earth' (Theogony 116–120).  The name may be older than Greek itself: a Linear B tablet from Knossos (Fp 14) appears to pair an offering 'to Tartaro' with offerings to the gods.  Homer adds the famous measurement: Tártaros lies as far beneath Hades as heaven is above earth, and a brazen anvil would fall nine days and nine nights before striking bottom (Iliad 8.

**The Titans Cast Down.** When the ten-year Titanomachy ended, Zeus hurled the defeated Titans down 'under the murky gloom of the misty darkness' — into Tártaros, where a bronze fence runs round it, Poseidon fixed gates of bronze, and the Hundred-Handers stand as guards 'beyond the gates, the faithful wardens' (Hesiod, Theogony 713–735).  The Iliad gives the scene from below: there the Titans sit at the threshold, 'a dreadful thing to hear' for any who would approach (Iliad 8. 478–481).

## Not the First Rebrand

The Romans transliterated the name directly as Tartarus and made it the lowest region of the underworld, a place of torment distinct from the neutral infernum.  In Virgil's Aeneid, the wicked are judged and cast into Tartarus, while the blessed ascend to Elysium. The office is only the latest translation.
